a.q: Which drive is met when a business gives staff clear and fair rules, and a secure job?
opts: Defend
Acquire
Bond
Learn
a.why: The drive to defend covers security and fairness. Acquire is the tempting wrong answer, but it is about gaining rewards such as pay, not about protection or fair treatment.

b.q: Ravi's Bendigo firm pays high bonuses and gives staff big status titles. Staff still seem flat. Teams rarely meet and the work is repetitive. What does the theory suggest?
opts: Bond and learn drives are unmet, so motivation is weaker
The acquire drive is unmet, so bonuses should rise
All four drives are met, because pay is high
Only the defend drive matters, so job security is needed
b.why: Bonuses and titles meet the drive to acquire, but rare team contact leaves bond unmet and repetitive work leaves learn unmet. The theory says motivation is best when all four are met, so high pay alone is not enough.

proposal.title: Lawrence and Nohria's four drive theory
card: Lawrence and Nohria said four drives shape how people act at work: the drives to acquire, to bond, to learn and to defend.
The drive to acquire is to gain things, such as pay, status and rewards. The drive to bond is to form connections with others, such as teammates and the business itself.
The drive to learn is to understand the world and grow through challenging, meaningful work. The drive to defend is to protect oneself and others, and to see fairness and security at work.
Lawrence and Nohria said a workplace that meets all four drives motivates staff best. Meeting only one or two, such as through pay alone, leaves motivation weaker.
proposal.remember: Motivation is strongest when a workplace meets all four drives, not just one.
